sentences.text: Shri Shiv Kumar Shrivastava- Government Advocate for th
This appeal is admitted for final hearing.

Heard on I.A. No.11326/2023 an application under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for suspension of sentence filed on behalf of the appellants.
Appellant no.1 has been convicted for the offences under Sections 149, 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year with fine of Rs.1,000/- for offences under section 149 of IPC, rigorous imprisonment for three years with fine of Rs.1,000/- for offences under section 420 of IPC, rigorous imprisonment for three years with fine of Rs.1,000/- for offences under section 467 of IPC, rigorous imprisonment for three years with fine of Rs.1,000/- for offences under section 468 of IPC and rigorous imprisonment for three years with fine of Rs.1,000/-
for offences under section 471 of IPC, with default stipulation.

Appellant no.2 has been convicted for the offences under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years with fine of Rs.1,000/- for offences under section 420 of IPC, rigorous imprisonment for three years with fine of Rs.1,000/- for offences under section 467 of IPC, rigorous imprisonment for three years with fine of Rs.1,000/- for offences under section 468 of IPC and rigorous imprisonment for three years with fine of Rs.1,000/-
for offences under section 471 of IPC, default stipulation.
The appellants have been on bail during trial.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits appellants are labourers and their sentences have been suspended till 06.06.2023.
Therefore, their sentences be suspended during the pendency of the appeal.
Trial will take time to conclude, hence, the sentence of the appellants may be suspended and they may be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State opposes the suspension application.

After hearing the learned counsel for the appellants and taking into consideration that they were on bail during the period of trial and have never misused the liberty granted to them, this Court is of the view that it is a fit case for suspension of sentence is made out in favour of the appellants.

I t is directed that on depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two sureties bonds in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for their appearance before the concerned Trial Court on 13.07.2023 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the concerned Trial Court, the appellants be released on bail and the substantive sentence under appeal shall remain suspended.
List for final hearing as per its turn and seniority in part B of the cause list.
Record of the trial Court be called for.
(VIVEK AGARWAL) V. JUDGE rk.
